Confidence intervals for native fit coefficients and GPCM slopes

Source: R/api-gpcm-intervals.R
confint.mfrm_fit.Rd

Compute pointwise Wald intervals for free coef(object) coordinates in native MML/CML fits (parm = NULL), positive GPCM discriminations and slope contrasts (parm = "slopes"), or two-family GPCM step offsets (parm = "steps"). Inspect attr(ci, "diagnostics") (CIEligible, CoverageQualified, InferenceReview) alongside returned bounds.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_fit'
confint(
  object,
  parm = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  scale = c("relative", "standardized"),
  contrasts = NULL,
  contrast_scale = c("ratio", "difference"),
  method = c("model", "sandwich", "profile"),
  clusters = NULL,
  adjust = FALSE,
  simultaneous = c("none", "bonferroni"),
  ...,
  slope = NULL,
  profile_control = list()
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_cml_fit'
confint(object, parm = NULL, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_comparison_fit'
confint(object, parm = NULL, level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

object

Native MML or CML fit_mfrm() result (JML structural intervals are unsupported).

parm

NULL (free coef(object) coordinates), character/integer subset, "slopes" (GPCM discriminations), or "steps" (two-family GPCM within-level step offsets).

level

Confidence level in (0, 1) (default 0.95).

scale

For parm = "slopes": "relative" (one-family default, geometric mean 1) or "standardized" (population SD times slope, including estimated-SD covariance; required default for two-family fits).

contrasts

Optional named zero-sum contrast matrix across slope levels and scale ("ratio" exponentiating log contrasts or "difference" via delta method).

contrast_scale

Optional named zero-sum contrast matrix across slope levels and scale ("ratio" exponentiating log contrasts or "difference" via delta method).

method

"model" (inverse full joint observed information), "sandwich" (Person/cluster marginal-likelihood score sandwich for one-family GPCM), or experimental "profile" (chi-square(1) deviance profile reoptimizing all nuisance parameters for one slope).

clusters

Optional Person-to-Cluster data.frame and G/(G - 1) factor (FALSE default) for method = "sandwich".

adjust

Optional Person-to-Cluster data.frame and G/(G - 1) factor (FALSE default) for method = "sandwich".

simultaneous

"none" (pointwise default) or "bonferroni" across rows in the current call.

...

Unused; additional arguments are rejected.

slope

Required target level for method = "profile" (e.g., "R01" or named c(Task = "t1") in two-family fits) and search budget list (maxit = 400, max_steps = 8, initial_step = 0.5).

profile_control

Required target level for method = "profile" (e.g., "R01" or named c(Task = "t1") in two-family fits) and search budget list (maxit = 400, max_steps = 8, initial_step = 0.5).

Value

Numeric Lower/Upper matrix (class mfrm_slope_intervals for parm = "slopes", or mfrm_facet_intervals for two-family parm = "steps") with diagnostics, checks, and method attributes.

Details

Free coefficients and GPCM slopes. Default coefficient intervals use \(\hat b_j \pm z_{(1+\mathrm{level})/2}\sqrt{V_{jj}}\) from qualified vcov(object). For parm = "slopes", free log-slope covariance \(V_\eta\) from the full joint observed information expands via \(J V_\eta J^\top\) to G sum-zero log slopes with bounds \(\exp(\log \hat a_g \pm z\,\mathrm{SE}(\log \hat a_g))\) (requiring quad_points >= 31, unit weights, positive unregularized curvature, and no marginal response-dimension rank deficit; dense Hessian allocation respects options(mfrmr.max_information_bytes = 256 * 1024^2)).

Two-family and profile checks. Two-family log-Wald and "steps" intervals differentiate the fitted fixed-grid EM or moving-node adaptive marginal objective, verifying SE-scaled score length \sqrt{g'Vg} <= 0.01 and 2*q - 1 quadrature stability (CIEligible vs CoverageQualified = FALSE). Profile intervals verify agreement of retained and neutral starts (<= 1e-5 NLL), positive-definite nuisance Hessians at both quadrature orders, and endpoint LR residuals <= 1e-4, storing scans in attr(ci, "profile") and Wald comparisons in attr(ci, "wald").

References

  • Fischer, S. M., & Lewis, M. A. (2021). Statistics and Computing, 31, 38. doi:10.1007/s11222-021-10012-y .

  • Zeileis, A., Koell, S., & Graham, N. (2020). J. Stat. Softw., 95(1), 1–36. doi:10.18637/jss.v095.i01 .

See also

mfrmr_output_guide(), mfrmr_gpcm_scope, bootstrap_mfrm_gpcm()

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("confint.mfrm_fit", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Compare intervals for free coefficients and relative discriminations.
# Reuse the synthetic GPCM fit; estimation uses 61 quadrature points.
# Full regeneration recipe: examples/measurement-fits.R in the package.
fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "measurement-fits.rds",
  package = "mfrmr", mustWork = TRUE))$gpcm
# The default matches coef(fit): steps, locations and log slopes.
coefficients_ci <- confint(fit, level = 0.95)
head(cbind(Estimate = coef(fit), coefficients_ci))
attr(coefficients_ci, "diagnostics") # Availability and interpretation
# Missing bounds do not erase retained points; report the reason too.
# Explicitly request positive relative slopes for rater comparison:
intervals <- confint(fit, parm = "slopes", level = 0.95)
intervals
attr(intervals, "diagnostics")[, c("SlopeFacet", "Estimate",
  "CIEligible", "InferenceReview")]
# Relative slopes have geometric mean one. A value above one means a
# steeper response curve, not greater severity or better rater quality.
# Missing bounds need the saved reason; availability is not a coverage test.
plot(intervals)
file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(intervals, file) # Use a lasting path for your analysis
saved <- readRDS(file)
apa_table(saved) # Reuse the intervals without fitting again

# A separate, prespecified profile calculation can be requested with
# confint(fit, parm = "slopes", method = "profile", slope = chosen_rater).
# Choose chosen_rater from fit$slopes$SlopeFacet; see the profile section.
} # }
